newsitem.title: PERU: Media owner condemns Peru after losing nationality.
newsitem.headline: Media owner condemns Peru after losing nationality.

text.p: The Israeli-born owner of Peru's Frecuencia Latina TV station expressed outrage on Monday at the government's weekend decision to revoke his local citizenship.

"This is a barbarity ... they are committing horrible abuses, first against my personal rights, then against my property," Baruch Ivcher said in a radio interview from Miami, where he was staying because of alleged political persecution and death threats.
Sunday's move against Ivcher triggered an instant wave of condemnation from the public and the national media, some of whom called for street protests.

"Independent journalism, institutions unbowed by the government's steam roller, and citizens at large, must close ranks in these circumstances and energetically protest to stop the escalating anti-democratic process," Peru's respected daily El Comercio said in an editorial.

The government cancelled Ivcher's citizenship because of alleged administrative "irregularities" including omissions in the application forms and lack of proof that he gave up his Israeli nationality. The documents were, however, signed and approved in 1984 by ex-President Fernando Belaunde, who denied on Monday there had been any irregularities.

Analysts said the timing of the measure against Ivcher was no coincidence following a string of stories by Frecuencia Latina alleging corruption and rights abuses in President Alberto Fujimori's security forces.
Attorney General Miguel Aljovin promised on Monday to investigate what media here have quickly dubbed "Limagate" in reference to the former U.S. President Richard Nixon's Watergate bugging scandal.
On a trip to the jungle city of Iquitos on Saturday, Fujimori pledged to "defend all the freedoms, the freedom of press, and the freedom of expression."
